description: A pre-motion numerical failure may follow one bounded authored recovery, or terminate if no legal alternative is available. A single route needs no Decisions approval. Use Decisions when choosing among different eligible remedies. Observation recovery applies to missing or stale sensing. Pure IK or collision rejection does not establish a visual limitation. Check candidates with the official GPU batched IK and BatchMotionPlanner.plan_grasp APIs. Plan approach, grasp and lift, with current robot/world geometry. The public three-phase SDK uses the executing arm Link3 and Link4 links during goalset/grasp/lift solving and restores them for approach. All four contact links are restored on return or exception. Exact command validation checks the environment, peer arm, non-contact links and the phase-specific target-contact policy. Closing and the post-lift measured attachment have separate checks. Validate endpoints and commands before execution. A finite destination preflight may reject a candidate whose sampled transport endpoints fail, but does not prove the whole destination infeasible. The actual holding attachment is not installed before lift. This skill plans only; a successful plan is neither a grasp nor a holding proof. CAD pregrasp lift bounds reuse the immutable canonical partition and sphere centres for identical model vertices, sphere budget and partition size. Each candidate still transforms every cell vertex and recomputes its enclosing radius with current padding. This is a geometric preview, not an installed attachment or a holding proof. Open-stop feedback noise within 1e-9 radians is normalized only in the planning model, with 1e-8 metres of conservative hand-sphere reserve; raw feedback and all larger closures are preserved. Task planning uses warmed fixed batches of two ranked candidates; rejected batches continue through the original remaining pool. Larger explicit requests keep their full size. Seeds, collision thresholds and endpoint/command validation are unchanged. For unknown OBB objects, complete numerical rejection of a frozen pool permits the next bounded GraspGen pool (256, 512, followed by four pools of 1000 requested candidates). Current scene binding and both-arm collision evidence are required, including CAD/OBB/cuboid worlds. Missing or indeterminate evidence stops the search; CAD libraries remain a single pool. No graph nodes or motion are added. planning_no_valid_candidate reports rejection of this arm's evaluated candidates before any motion, with planner/endpoint/contact/command details. It does not prove another arm infeasible. Any changed-input recovery must be authored in the graph. pool_exhaustion.scope=internal_frozen_candidate_pool and outcome=pool_expansion_not_permitted limit internal sampling only, not graph-level recovery. Source-container lift neighbors come from enabled, validated published CAD/OBB bounds overlapping the source XY envelope, including retained obstacles. Historical input siblings and completed_target_ids are not a geometry source. Retired inputs are not queried for current measurements; any still-published enabled obstacle remains conservative collision evidence. Target retirement, scene binding, rim height, held-envelope clearance and full trajectory checks remain enforced. source_support_current is a data prerequisite established by identify_target after the latest observe_scene. Reobservation updates geometry but does not automatically refresh semantic support. Author restoration of this prerequisite in any observation recovery path before replanning. MotionPlanBinding binds target, destination, arm, generation, observation, scene and settings; execution checks it before physical commands. During grasp descent and closure, the executing Link3 fingers and Link4 linkage may contact the selected target. Contact-link/environment, peer-arm, other-link/target and self-collision checks retain their configured clearance. Unknown-object grasp endpoints must provide full-cloud clearance from the authored fully-open pad collision mesh convex hulls, using the existing measurement uncertainty and collision margin. A finite, model-bound negative clearance rejects that candidate before motion and permits continuation of the existing bounded search. The achieved trajectory endpoint FK is used for bounded closure contact prediction. Reports distinguish zero source IK successes from successful IK candidates rejected by application gripper/contact prerequisites. Per-round source IK counts and rejection reasons are retained for graph recovery judgments.
capability: Check candidates with the official GPU batched IK and BatchMotionPlanner.plan_grasp APIs
